title: Neural Dual Bounds: Valid-by-Construction JGLP Warm-Starts for MAP and Constrained MAP
claim: Warm-starting an iterative optimizer from a one-pass learned solution starts closer to the optimum and converges faster than zero initialization.
layout: 3 panels in a row, same axes, green star marks warm-start point
description: Three side-by-side line plots, one each for BN_12, grid20x20.f10 and Segmentation_14. The x-axis is JGLP iterations from 0 to 200. The y-axis is the dual objective D(θ, m). Each panel has a blue curve for zero-init and a red curve for neural-init. Both curves decay toward a dotted horizontal line marking the optimum D*, whose value is given in the legend. A large green star at iteration 0 marks the standalone neural bound (0.04 ms). It sits well below the blue curve's starting point and at the start of the red curve. The red curve stays below the blue one throughout. The gap is largest early on. In the Segmentation panel the two curves merge after about 40 iterations. The eye goes first to the green star and the gap between the red and blue curves at the left of each panel. Legends are in the top right of each panel.
caption: JGLP convergence with and without neural warm-start on three representative PGMs (BN\_12, grid20$\times$20.f10, Segmentation\_14). Both curves provably converge to the same optimum $D^*$ since $D(\boldsymbol{\theta}, m)$ is convex in $m$. The green star marks the standalone neural bound from a single forward pass ($\sim\!0.04$ ms on GPU) and is used as the warm-start for JGLP at iteration 0; it starts strictly below zero-init and reaches a small neighborhood of $D^*$ in fewer JGLP iterations. The three panels span the BN, Grid, and Segmentation families; full results across all 37 PGMs are reported in Appendix [ref] and Table [ref].
abstract: We present Neural Dual Bounds, a calibration-free framework that produces deterministic upper bounds for MAP inference in probabilistic graphical models using a single neural-network forward pass. The framework trains a network to output the edge messages of a mini-bucket style upper bound on a given join-graph decomposition in a self-supervised manner by directly minimizing a smooth dual objective. The output of this network can be used at test time to warm-start a standard JGLP optimizer. Across diverse benchmarks, this warm start yields dual gaps that are orders of magnitude tighter than those from zero initialization, with the largest gains in the early-iteration regime. We also apply our framework for the constrained MAP (CMPE) task, where neural warm starts with test-time adaptation are comparable to the adaptive baseline on Bayesian networks and achieve the tightest dual gaps, by one to two orders of magnitude, on the grid and segmentation families.
